title: Pitch link to pitch plate grip length
description: Built from scratch against the drawings and the NAS standards. Two of its six elements carry a band no document in this repo can be re-read for, applied 2026-09-15 by operator ruling and marked untraced rather than omitted.

joint.zone_note: printed zone of the DETAIL B caption on the 2026-AUG-3 export; the view body sits above it, spanning printed J3-K4. Slice 1 cited I6 for the same caption on the 2026-JUL-23 POST export -- a view's printed zone is not stable across exports (see the worksheet, finding F4).
joint.description: The 5-place joint in DETAIL B: NAS6403U11D bolt down through the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing) and a plain bushing, through a 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, retained by a slotted nut + cotter pin over a flat washer. DETAIL B shows TWO grip stacks of identical architecture: this one (5 places, -11 bolt) and the tangential-link joint analysed in slice 1 (3 places, -14 bolt).

parts.role: bolt, .190-32 x .688 grip, unplated, drilled shank
plain bushing, .1900 in ID x .1875 in long (8 = 3 tangential-link places + 5 here)
PITCH PLATE ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW -- contains the 215197 pitch plate

joint.clamped: The bolt clamps, in order from its head: the 214820-002 bushing, the pitch-link eye (unsourced -- see gaps), the 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, and the NAS1149V0332H washer. Retention is the MS9363-09 slotted nut with an MS24665-153 cotter pin through the drilled shank ('D' suffix, NAS6403 sheet 2 CODE block).
joint.question: Does the NAS6403U11D (.688 in grip) work in this joint -- i.e. does the end of its full cylindrical shank clear the nut bearing face (JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5), and does its cotter hole sit clear of the clamped stack?
joint.scope: Grip length only, and only along the bolt axis. Out of scope, deliberately: diameter and hole fits (simple two-component fits); bushing-to-bore interference (JPS00176); the pitch link's own internal stack; the joint at the other end of the pitch link; torque and preload.
joint.identification_note: No part in the 217755 parts list is named 'pitch link'. This joint is identified as Jeff's 'pitch link to pitch plate' by elimination and corroboration, not by nomenclature: (1) his note says the joint is visible in the same view as the tangential-link joint, and DETAIL B contains exactly two grip stacks; (2) slice 1 claimed the 3X / -14 stack as the tangential link, matching 212956-005 PITCH ANTI ROTATION LINK ASSEMBLY at qty 3; (3) this one is 5 places, the propeller has FIVE blades (217755 sheet 2 FRONT VIEW), and one pitch link per blade gives five; (4) the pitch plate part drawing 215197 carries a distinct 5X 4.06 +/-0.10 flange group, separate from the 3X +/-0.08 (tangential) and 1X +/-0.10 (VPA) groups. The link part number itself is gap 1.

checks.label: shank out, NAS6403U11D
excluded_terms: pitch-link eye / spherical bearing width -- no document
checks.guidance: clamped column minus grip. Negative means the end of the full cylindrical shank sits proud of the nut bearing face, so the nut would engage incomplete threads -- which JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5 forbids outright ('The nut, nutplate, insert, part body, etc., shall not engage any incomplete threads of the bolt shank'). This check carries `complete: false`: the pitch-link eye is missing from the column, so its verdict is scoped to the budget, not to the joint, and the verdict below is not a design conclusion. Read the magnitude instead -- it is the pitch-link eye width the joint REQUIRES. The BINDING requirement is the worst-case end: eye >= 8.4280 mm (grip at max 17.7292 against the column at min 9.3012) to pass worst case, and >= 7.8424 mm to pass at nominal, so an eye between 7.8424 and 8.4280 mm makes this check `marginal`. The other worst-case end, 7.3868 mm (grip at min against the column at max), is the value below which the check fails even in the most favourable combination -- it is NOT the requirement. Sourcing that one number flips this check. These three numbers WIDENED on 2026-09-15 (handoff pitch_link_known_bands) when the bushing and washer bands were applied: the binding requirement moved 8.1939 -> 8.4280 and the marginal window from 0.354 mm wide to 0.586 mm. Two of the three terms in the column are `untraced`, so the requirement is only as good as a workbook cell and an operator's screenshot.

checks.label: cotter hole clear of the clamped column

configuration.nut: MS9363-09 slotted -- height and castellation geometry unsourced

excluded_terms: pitch-link eye / spherical bearing width -- no document
checks.guidance: Head-to-cotter-hole minus the sourced clamped column. What is left over must cover the pitch-link eye PLUS the nut's thread-start-to-castellation distance; both are unsourced, so this is a budget, not a verdict on the joint. It passes with 11.0444 mm worst case available (11.1435 before the 2026-09-15 bands were applied). It cannot settle the joint: with a slotted nut and a cotter pin the constraint is slot-vs-hole ALIGNMENT, which quantises acceptable grip -- see the notes and the worksheet.

notes: BUILT FROM SCRATCH. No source workbook exists for this joint, so there is no re-derivation section in the worksheet, no `workbook_cells` on any path or check, and no `[NOT IN WORKBOOK]` markers -- every check here is original. What is NO LONGER true, as of 2026-09-15: `kind: "workbook"` appeared zero times, and now appears exactly once (`washer_nas1149v0332`). SOP Step 5b's amendment of the same date is what permits it -- a sourced-but-unverified value may be applied with its true confidence carried and displayed, and the same part+feature must carry the same band in every stack that uses it. See `provenance.source_note`.

THE STACK IS INCOMPLETE AND SAYS SO. The pitch-link eye / spherical bearing width is not in any document available here, so it is NOT modelled as an element with invented or recalled numbers -- it is a named gap, and the two checks are written so that the missing value appears as an explicit budget. Nothing in this file was filled from memory.

NO ZERO-WIDTH BAND REMAINS, AND TWO BANDS ARE UNVERIFIED. Until 2026-09-15 `bushing_214820` and `washer_nas1149v0332` carried min == max == nominal, which made every interval here a LOWER bound on the true spread. Jeff opened the 214820-002 drawing, found a real 4.76 +0.00/-0.13 where the viewer was showing +/-0, and ruled that a sourced-but-unverified number belongs in the stack loudly rather than omitted silently. Both now carry their band and both carry `confidence: "untraced"`, which is what a reader and the viewer must key on: the intervals are no longer lower bounds, and they are no longer re-checkable inside this repo either. Their sources -- an operator's screenshot of a drawing that is not here, and a cell in a workbook that is -- are named in each element's notes and remain ranked gaps 3 and 4.

ONE ASYMMETRIC BAND, AND IT MOVES THE RSS CENTRE OFF THE NOMINAL. `bushing_214820` is 4.76 +0.00/-0.13: its nominal IS its max, so its midpoint (4.695) is not its nominal. `fold()` combines half-ranges in quadrature about the MIDPOINT, so from 2026-09-15 `rss_center != nominal` on `clamped_stack_sourced` (9.5678 vs 9.6328) and on both checks, by exactly the 0.065 mm half-offset of that one element. This stack's notes and worksheet previously said the re-centering artefact did not occur here; it does now. It is an artefact of the fold model, not a second opinion about the joint -- verdicts never read RSS (`CheckResult.verdict` cannot see it), and the worst-case columns are unaffected.

NO INVERTING ELEMENT EXISTS HERE. Every element is an additive external length or a hole location; there is no chamfer, relief or counterbore, so `max == mmc` on all five elements that carry lmc/mmc (three until 2026-09-15, when the bushing and washer gained bands and with them a material condition), and `cotter_hole_from_point` carries neither, because it is a location and 'most material' has no meaning for where a hole sits. That is not the naive-MMC-mapping smell the review checklist warns about -- it is the absence of a subtracted material feature. The only negative signs in this file are on whole-element/whole-path subtractions.

QUANTISED GRIP -- THE MODEL DOES NOT SETTLE THIS JOINT. Retention is MS9363-09 (NUT, SLOTTED, HEXAGON, SHEAR) plus MS24665-153 cotter pin through the drilled shank. The governing constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the bolt's cotter hole, which quantises acceptable grip into discrete workable values instead of bounding it in a continuous interval. JPS00094 Rev C section 5.9.7 states the remedy in as many words -- 'If the hole and nut castellation do not align, change/add a washer or a different nut, and try again' with a footnote that 'Different nuts likely have different manufactured thread-start to castellation-hole spacing' -- and section 5.5.3.a caps the remedy at three washers per fastener. So this is assembly-time selection by specification, and no grip interval computed here can replace it. The two documents that would close it: MS9363 (slot count and depth) and the nut height; the bolt side is already closed by NAS6403 sheet 1 M = .174/.154.

Element order is the physical order from the bolt head: bushing, [pitch-link eye -- MISSING], pitch-plate lug, washer; the three fastener dimensions follow. Only the path term lists are load-bearing for the arithmetic.
